title: Codify provenance gate and profile release broker for model onboarding
creator: Asha Verma
description:
Background:
Redwood needs an automated, auditable path from CI builds -> signed artifacts -> performance-profile verification -> catalog promotion. Current onboarding steps are a mix of manual steps and brittle scripts; this ticket will codify a "profile release broker": a lightweight orchestrator that receives build artifacts, attaches provenance (SBOM, sigs, Rekor entry), runs profile verification jobs, and atomically moves artifacts from staging to the public model catalog with optional version pinning and canary labels.

Goals / Scope:
- Implement a release broker service that integrates with our CI (Buildkite) and artifact storage (s3://redwood-models-staging).
- Use sigstore/fulcio + Rekor for signing and immutable log entries; record SBOM + performance profile outputs as provenance metadata.
- Automate running the perf-profile test suite and gating promotion on profile pass + threshold checks (latency P95 within X%, throughput target).
- Support automatic version pinning for customers that opt into a "pinned" channel and create canonical release tags for unpinned channels.
- Publish a machine-readable published-profile manifest to the model catalog service and provide revertability (rollback tag).
- Expose clear audit trail links in the catalog UI (build log, signature, Rekor timestamp, perf report).

Non-goals:
- Large refactor of runtime serving engine. This is about release automation and provenance, not model binary internals.

Success criteria / acceptance criteria:
1) A Buildkite pipeline change triggers the release broker on successful build and test, and the broker writes a signed Rekor entry containing artifact digest and SBOM.
2) The perf-profile test runner executes automatically against the staging artifact; results are stored and surfaced as a JSON profile blob.
3) The broker enforces configurable gates: e.g., "profile_pass==true" and "p95_latency_delta <= 10%" before allowing promotion.
4) Promotion publishes the artifact to s3://redwood-models/releases/<model>/<version>/ and updates the model catalog with provenance links and the pinned version if configured.
5) UI shows the promoted release with links to buildkite logs, GitHub PR, Rekor entry, and profile report.
6) Rollback path works: a single API call reassigns the catalog pointer to the previous pinned digest and records a reversal event.
7) End-to-end tests / integration test harness verifies gating behavior in CI and is included in the pipeline.

High-level implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (design + PoC, 2 weeks): design broker API spec, define required provenance fields (artifact_digest, sbom_url, signatures, rekor_id, profile_blob_url), and build a minimal PoC that accepts a signed artifact and writes Rekor entry.
- Phase 2 (perf integration, 2 weeks): implement perf-profile runner adapter that runs existing perf harness against staging artifact and uploads JSON results.
- Phase 3 (gating & promotion, 2 weeks): implement gate config, promotion steps to releases bucket, catalog update API call, and UI hooks for audit links.
- Phase 4 (tests + rollout, 1 week): integration tests, staged rollout to internal teams, add monitoring and alerting for failed promotions.

Engineering tasks (top-level):
- Broker service: API + worker loop to reconcile pending promotions. (ENG-16112)
- Sigstore integration: signing flow in CI and Rekor submission library. (ENG-16113)
- Perf runner adapter: orchestrate perf-profile jobs and upload artifacts.
- Catalog update client: safe atomic update semantics with optimistic locking and revert API.
- CI changes: Buildkite pipeline hooks and environment variables for signing and staging artifacts.
- UI: surface provenance links and a "promote" button with gating info.
- E2E tests: simulate failing profiles, partial signatures, and rollback scenarios.

Security & compliance notes:
- All attestation artifacts (SBOMs, profile results) must be stored with encryption at rest and restricted ACLs; Rekor entries provide immutability for signing assertions.
- Access to promotion actions controlled by RBAC (console role required).
- Threat: supply-chain attack where signed artifact does not match uploaded object; mitigate by validating artifact digest at promotion time and verifying Rekor/sigstore record.

Rollout strategy:
- Start with internal-only model onboarding (dev-team models) and promote a few low-risk models automatically.
- Monitor promotion failure rate, profile rejection rate, and catalog updates for 2 weeks.
- Open a migration path for existing manually-published artifacts to be re-ingested into the broker with recorded provenance.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- What is the canonical schema for the profile_blob? (Suggest JSON fields: p95_ms, p50_ms, throughput_tps, memory_mb, test_seed, workload_spec_url)
- Do we require sigstore for all builds including PR preview builds, or only for release builds?
- Pinning policy: should automatic pinning be opt-in per-customer (catalog-level) or opt-out?

Longer-term ideas (out of scope for this ticket but to consider):
- Integrate with Optimize to suggest quantization/profile tradeoffs before promotion.
- Add cryptographic attestation of runtime execution (for on-prem proofs).
